newsitem.title: USA: DNA to play major role in NY rape case.
newsitem.headline: DNA to play major role in NY rape case.

text.p: A New York fisherman, freed from prison five years ago after DNA evidence cleared him of rape, went on trial on Wednesday on another rape charge.
Kerry Kotler, 39, is accused of raping and kidnapping a 20-year-old college student in August 1995.

He spent 11 years in prison on a rape charge before DNA evidence helped overturn his conviction. He won an unlawful imprisonment lawsuit against New York state and was negotiating a monetary settlement when he was arrested on this charge.

In this case, said Suffolk County, New York prosecutor Randall Hinrichs, DNA evidence would prove Kotler was the man who followed the student from a resort beach bar, flagged her down with a phony police badge and convinced her to follow him to a remote area.
There, he forced her to undress and he raped her, the prosecutor said. Kotler then used a water bottle in an attempt to wash traces of his semen from her body, he said.
But DNA recovered from fluids on her body nevertheless showed Kotler was the culpirt, the prosecutor said.
Defence attorney Jack Litman said he would not contest any finding that it was Kotler's semen.
But he said the fisherman was framed by local police who stole used condoms or underwear from his garbage, he argued.
The police were embarrassed and angry over his release in the earlier case, the defence attorney said.
In the earlier case, Kotler was convicted of raping a mother of three children in 1978 and again in 1981.
Attorneys Barry Scheck and Peter Neufeld helped win Kotler's freedom, and they went on to become specialists in DNA evidence.

Scheck and Neufeld were part of the legal team that defended former football star O.J. Simpson, and they tried to discredit the genetic evidence in his case. Simpson was cleared of the murders of his ex-wife and her friend.
No matter what the outcome of this trial, Kotler is expected to be awarded more than $1 million from his lawsuit against the state.
The victim in this case saw a partial license plate that police traced to Kotler's girlfriend, the prosecutor said.
Police also found a dog hair on the victim's clothing that is consistent with that of Kotler's German Shepherd, he said.
The victim is scheduled to testify about her ordeal on Thursday in Suffolk County court before Judge Morton Weissman.
Defence attorneys say the description she gave police of her attacker did not match Kotler.
